marks.q: As we enter Q4 we are mindful of external pressures, including the Omicron variant and supply chain constraints, although our better than expected Q3 trading means we expect full year profit to be slightly ahead of consensus estimate.
However, given our progress year to date we expect our full year revenue and adjusted operating profit margin to be ahead of the top end of the current consensus range.
As reported on 30 March 2022, we expect our full year adjusted operating profit margin to be at the top end of the consensus range2.

Despite the external challenges, we remain confident in driving further market share gains, improving operating efficiencies, delivering ongoing adjusted operating profit margin growth and generating long-term sustainable value.
Given our strength in the first quarter, we now expect our full year revenue and profit to be slightly ahead of current consensus estimates1.

Given our strong trading performance year to date we expect our full year revenue and adjusted profit before tax to be slightly ahead of current consensus estimates1, albeit with a greater first half weighting than historically delivered.
Notwithstanding the tougher global economic environment, trading remains in line with our and consensus expectations for the full year.
The Company has delivered another strong revenue and profit performance in the first half and trading over the first four weeks of the second half has been in line with our expectations.
Given our performance year to date we expect our full year adjusted profit before tax to be towards the top end of current consensus estimates1.
We expect our full year revenue to be in line with consensus estimates but our adjusted operating profit to be slightly ahead reflecting gross margin benefits and strong cost control.

Despite this more uncertain economic environment and the strong comparator period last year, we are comfortable with current consensus profit expectations5 for 2023/24, albeit with performance more weighted to the second half.
Trading for the quarter was marginally softer than anticipated, reflecting the more difficult macroeconomic backdrop and tough comparatives.
RS has delivered a resilient performance in difficult markets, which have been more challenging than anticipated at the beginning of the year.
Q3 trading was challenging reflecting the difficult economic backdrop, geopolitical uncertainty, weak industrial and electronic markets and customer surplus inventory in electronics.

During this period of investment, we expect some short-term dilution to our operating profit margin reflecting a partial resumption of our employee annual incentive, ongoing cost inflation, annualisation of Distrelec costs and the additional c. £15 million organic investment announced today.

Trading in the first quarter was in line with expectations. Group revenue grew 3% over the same period in the prior year and declined by 3% on a like-for-like basis, excluding acquisitions, foreign currency and trading days.

As a result, whilst short-term trading visibility remains limited, we will continue to flex the cost base appropriately and expect the outcome for the full year 2024/25 to be in line with current market expectations.
The softer than expected Q3 revenue performance and weak business confidence in EMEA will however likely result in full year profit before tax being around the bottom end of the consensus range4.
We are focusing on what we can control in markets that remain challenging, and we will continue to be agile in our execution and cost management whilst investing selectively for the future.
The Group continues to make good operational progress and our full year outlook is unchanged.
I'm pleased our performance in the first half of the year was in line with expectations and our full year outlook is unchanged.

As a result, despite revenue being lower than anticipated, through a solid gross margin performance, improved efficiency and disciplined cost control, we still expect adjusted profit before tax to be marginally ahead of market expectations1,3.
With our ongoing investment and greater agility, we see improving momentum into 2026/27 and most of our major markets are now back into low single digit growth.
marks.gnote: early signal: first step up in tone

marks.q: This, combined with strong execution of our multi-year improvement plan, is delivering good progress across all regions, as we anticipated at the start of the year.
As a result, our performance was ahead of our expectations and well ahead of the prior period, in part due to easier comparatives.

lines.text: Full-year view: last year “our full year outlook is unchanged”, Nov-24 “expect the outcome for the full year 2024/25 to be in line with current market expectations” → this year “trading momentum remains encouraging”; “ahead of our expectations” covers H1 only, with no full-year statement against expectations or the £263m consensus printed beside it
lines.span: Full-year anchor at Nov-22, Nov-24, Nov-25 → gap at Nov-26, despite the H1 beat

lines.text: Cost guide: May-26 “we expect inflation on our ongoing operating cost base to be 3%, variable costs to be 6% of revenue, continued build of employee incentive to be c. £5-£10 million and cost savings to be £10-15 million” → Nov-26 one net line, “to grow at approximately 7%, net of cost savings”; the “remains unchanged” list covers only “organic investment, restructuring and integration costs and capital expenditure”
lines.span: May-26 → Nov-26; inflation, incentive and savings no longer stated separately

lines.text: Quarterly like-for-like: Nov-25 “First quarter like-for-like revenue was down 2%” and “Group like-for-like revenue in the second quarter was up 1%” → Nov-26 half only, “like-for-like revenue was up 7%”, no Q1/Q2 split, so no exit rate as comparators toughen
lines.span: Q1 figure given at Jul-24, Jul-25 AGMs and Nov-25 → none at Jul-26 or Nov-26

lines.text: Growth accelerators: May-26 “Our growth accelerators outperformed the wider Group”, Nov-25 highlights “like-for-like revenue up 4% for RS PRO and up 7% for service solutions” → Nov-26 highlights “Strategic growth accelerators continue to deliver”, no figures; the body shows digital 5%, services and solutions 6%, RS PRO 5%, all below Group 7%
lines.span: Outperformed Group at May-25, May-26 → behind Group in H1 2026/27, numbers out of highlights
